facts.name: Symphonic Distribution
facts.cost: USD 29.99 (Starter, year 1) + USD 10/month Beatport add-on x 12 = USD 120.00. Year-one total = USD 149.99. Royalty splits to both remixers cost USD 0. Streaming royalties kept at 100%, so no commission drag. Highest sticker price of the DIY tier, but the only one where Beatport AND Traxsource both arrive as part of a normal, non-gated product.

distribution.model: Annual subscription. Starter = USD 29.99/year for one primary artist, unlimited releases, unlimited featuring and remixer artists. Beatport/Traxsource delivery is a 'specialty partner' add-on at USD 10/month on top. Symphonic Partner tier is a custom revenue-share deal, free to distribute, by approval only.
distribution.royalty_share: 100% of DSP streaming royalties on Starter (Symphonic takes no cut of Spotify/Apple/Deezer/Pandora revenue). YouTube Content ID is the exception: 30% collection fee. Partner tier is a negotiated percentage.
distribution.catches: Symphonic's FAQ states that a release distributed through Symphonic cannot be re-distributed via another distributor until the end of the contractual term — and the FAQ does NOT state what that term is. The Beatport add-on is a recurring monthly charge that must keep running for the release to stay on Beatport. YouTube Content ID at 30% is a steep collection fee. Starter is capped at one primary artist.

facts.summary: The unsigned electronic act that needs genuine Beatport and Traxsource delivery plus free multi-party splits, and is willing to accept an unpublished contract term in exchange.
facts.verify: Pricing and partner-store delivery read from the distributor's own pricing and partner pages (Aug 2026); prices change — re-check before signing up

facts.name: DistroKid
facts.cost: Musician USD 24.99 (year 1) + Beatport add-on USD 9.99/month x 12 = USD 119.88. Year-one total = USD 144.87. Splits to both remixers cost USD 0. If they want the second artist name (duo alias) on its own profile, Musician Plus instead: USD 44.99 + USD 119.88 = USD 164.87. Note the Beatport add-on is billed monthly and is 4.8x the cost of the base plan itself.

distribution.model: Annual subscription, unlimited uploads. Musician = USD 24.99/year (1 artist or band). Musician Plus = USD 44.99/year (2 artists or bands). Ultimate = USD 89.99/year (1-100 artists). Beatport is a paid 'Album Extra' at USD 9.99 per month.
distribution.catches: Add-ons are individually cheap but priced per song, per album, per year, so a growing catalogue quietly inflates the bill. Musician tier is one artist/band only, which matters if the duo ever wants separate project names. No publishing administration and no Traxsource.

facts.summary: Cost-sensitive artists who want the cheapest possible base subscription and free splits, and can stomach paying nearly USD 120/year extra just to reach Beatport.
facts.verify: Pricing and partner-store delivery read from the distributor's own pricing and partner pages (Aug 2026); prices change — re-check before signing up

facts.name: TuneCore
facts.city: Brooklyn, New York, USA (owned by Believe, Paris)
facts.cost: Rising Artist USD 24.99 (year 1) + Beatport USD 7.99/month billed annually = USD 95.88. Subtotal USD 120.87. Splits require the two remixers to hold accounts: each needs either an Unlimited plan or the Splits Collaborator subscription at USD 7.99/year. If the act covers both: 2 x USD 7.99 = USD 15.98. Year-one total = USD 136.85. Note: TuneCore Splits is unavailable on the pay-per-release model, so the USD 24.99 Single option cannot pay the remixers.

distribution.model: Hybrid. Unlimited annual plans: Rising Artist USD 24.99/year, Breakout Artist USD 44.99/year, Professional USD 54.99/year (+USD 14.99 per additional artist profile). Pay-per-release alternative: Single USD 24.99 one-time, Album USD 44.99 first year then USD 56.49/year thereafter. Beatport delivery is an extra USD 7.99/month, billed annually, and requires an Unlimited plan.
distribution.royalty_share: Artists 'keep 100% ownership and control' of recording revenue on the distribution plans. Exception explicitly stated on the pricing page: a 20% fee on social platform earnings (TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube).
distribution.catches: The 20% social-platform fee is a real cut on TikTok/Reels revenue, which is where an emerging act actually gets traction. Album pay-per-release jumps from USD 44.99 to USD 56.49/year after year one. Splits are blocked entirely on pay-per-release. Stop paying and releases come down.

facts.summary: Artists who want Believe's infrastructure and a clear upgrade path into Believe artist services, and don't mind their Beatport releases carrying TuneCore's label name.
facts.verify: Pricing and partner-store delivery read from the distributor's own pricing and partner pages (Aug 2026); prices change — re-check before signing up

facts.name: CD Baby
facts.cost: Released as one multi-track release (original + 2 remixes): USD 14.99 one-time = year-one total USD 14.99. Released as three separate singles: 3 x USD 9.99 = USD 29.97. Either way, CD Baby then keeps 9% of every dollar of streaming revenue permanently — so at, say, USD 5,000 of lifetime streaming income the real cost is USD 14.99 + USD 450 = USD 464.99, versus USD 149.99/year flat at Symphonic with Beatport included. The commission, not the upfront fee, is the actual price. And none of it reaches Beatport.

distribution.model: Per-release one-time fee plus permanent commission. Single USD 9.99 one-time. Album USD 14.99 one-time. No annual or subscription fees at all. CD Baby then retains 9% of digital distribution revenue in perpetuity.
distribution.royalty_share: 91% to the artist. CD Baby retains 9% of digital distribution revenue, forever, with no way to buy it out. Paid weekly.
distribution.catches: No Beatport at all. No automatic collaborator payment system, so two remixers means manual accounting and manual transfers, which is exactly how relationships with remixers go wrong.

facts.summary: Artists who want music online permanently with zero renewal risk and may press physical product — but not electronic acts who need Beatport.
facts.verify: Pricing and partner-store delivery read from the distributor's own pricing and partner pages (Aug 2026); prices change — re-check before signing up
